issues.issue: Do the 2020 'restoring' contributions make the $71,147 withdrawal a nontaxable rollover?
issues.diagnosis: Rerun 2c5b6354943: encoded as rollovers {distribution 71,147, rolledOver 71,147 (amount not stated; full amount assumed, an upper bound), days 366 (lower bound: 2018 distribution, 2020 deposit), fromIra false, no waiver}. The court did not apply a 60-day analysis expressly ('neither argued nor established the applicability of an exception'), but the outcome follows.

issues.issue: Is petitioners liable for the 10% sec. 72(t) additional tax on the early distributions?
issues.diagnosis: Mr. Ghaly under 59 1/2, no exception proven: 10% x 115,325 = 11,532.50 -> 11,533. The sec. 72(t)(2)(B) medical-expense exception failed on proof of payment (judgment on evidence); encoded with no exceptions as the court found.
issues.snippet: The withdrawal does not fit within any of the statutory exceptions, and the entire distribution is subject to the 10% additional tax.

issues.diagnosis: Opinion does not state the reported income. With an assumed as-filed MFJ AGI of 139,100 (taxable 115,100), adding 115,325 raises regular tax by 26,680 (49,900 x 22% + 65,425 x 24%) and the sec. 72(t) tax adds 11,533: total 38,213. The base is fitted, not found (any base within roughly $25 gives the same result), so this only shows the notice is consistent with full inclusion plus the 10% tax.
issues.snippet: determined a deficiency in petitioners' federal income tax of $ 38,213 and a section 6662(a) accuracy -related penalty of $4,797

notes: Decision for respondent on the full $38,213 deficiency; the sec. 6662(a) penalty was conceded by respondent (not encoded). The notice penalty fits: 20% x (38,213 - 14,229 withholding) = 4,796.80 -> 4,797, i.e. the underpayment was the deficiency net of the 1099-R withholding not claimed on the return. Filing status MFJ inferred from the joint petition. Case 2 in the case.json is a fitted proxy, not a finding.
